workItem.title: Restore five Runtime acceptance scenarios under secure mode

requirements.statement: The five Runtime acceptance scenarios (git-delivery, git-delivery-e2e, quality-apply, quality-state-consistency, quality-readback) pass while the Runtime stays in secure mode.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each of the five npm run accept:* scripts exits 0.
No script sets PRAXIS_SECURITY_MODE=compatibility or removes an approval check.
Every protected write the scripts perform runs through the real secure verification path (signature, expiry, ledger) with an ephemeral test key.

requirements.statement: Approval is not weakened by the repaired scenarios: a protected write without a valid signed authorization is still refused, and the test signer cannot be used outside an explicit test harness.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each scenario (or the shared helper test) shows an unsigned or wrongly signed write is refused with an APPROVAL_* code.
The test signer refuses to start without PRAXIS_TEST_ALLOW_SAME_IDENTITY=1 and uses only an ephemeral key and a temporary ledger.
The test signer never reads operator key paths or PRAXIS_APPROVAL_PRIVATE_KEY from the environment.

services.name: Runtime acceptance harness
responsibilities: Run protected writes in acceptance scripts under real signed authorizations from an ephemeral test signer

openQuestions: Should the test signer live in praxis-core (shared with other repos) or stay in praxis-runtime/tools/scripts?
risks: Same-user host: an in-process test signer is not an independent broker, so the scenarios prove the verification path, not OS-level isolation.
handoffs.notes: Failures were reproduced before this handoff: git-delivery and git-delivery-e2e stop with APPROVAL_ISOLATION_UNAVAILABLE (broker-not-configured); quality-apply, quality-state-consistency and quality-readback stop with APPROVAL_REQUIRED (direct mutation is not authorized) while seeding a mock Jira.

risks: Same-user host: an in-process test signer is not an independent broker, so the scenarios prove the verification path, not OS-level isolation.

decisionRecords.statement: Add one shared acceptance helper, tools/scripts/test-broker.mjs, that creates an ephemeral signing key and temporary ledger, runs fixture setup and library calls under real signed authorizations through the existing secure verification path, and is the only place that sets PRAXIS_TEST_ALLOW_SAME_IDENTITY. The five scripts use it; no product security code changes.
decisionRecords.rationale: Root cause is in the scripts, not the product: they call protected library writes and seed a mock Jira directly, which secure mode correctly refuses. A shared signer keeps signature, expiry and ledger checks real; compatibility mode would skip them. Keeping it in praxis-runtime avoids a new cross-repo dependency; Core already exposes the signing primitives.

implementationUnits.summary: Ephemeral test signer (test-broker.mjs + test-broker.test.mjs) and the five acceptance scripts ported to it. Git delivery and e2e run in-process writes under signed authorizations; their packaged-MCPB phases now prove unsigned protected calls are refused and mark the signed positive path BLOCKED. quality-apply/state-consistency/readback seed the mock tracker and call applyQualityReview under signed authorizations; quality-apply step N uses a stored host approval plus a signed token.

history.note: accept:git-delivery, accept:git-delivery-e2e, accept:quality-apply, accept:quality-state-consistency and accept:quality-readback fail because they predate secure-by-default mutation approval. Restore them without compatibility mode, without weakening approval and without real operator keys.
